name: The Tithe Courier
bio: The Tallymen collector's courier on the Delta round: carries the tithe-book's copies to Tollmere, and this morning carries one page south instead, with a face gone grey.
lore: Nobody at Moreva knows his name, which is how the Tallymen like their couriers. He is only ever seen from behind, a field ahead on the road, walking.
unique_habit: Never looks back, and never stops, until the top of the Hushline Stair.

appearance.notes: a Tallymen's slate-grey coat gone greyer, a buckled satchel, the brass tally at the belt

notes: Seen only as a lead (Leads, The Unsaid Page): gone from the world as a person, always, so he is never stood up to be spoken to. His def dresses the lead.

name: Brannock Tole
bio: The Tallymen's collector on the Delta round: comes to Moreva the night before tithe-day with his strongbox, his book and his bravo, sleeps on the boards beside the box so that nobody can open it without stepping over him, and takes the eels by the basket in the morning.
lore: Brannock Tole has collected the Delta for eleven years and has never once been robbed, which he puts down to sleeping light. Moreva puts it down to nobody having wanted anything he had until now.
unique_habit: Sleeps sitting half up against his strongbox with one hand on his waistcoat pocket, and talks sums in his sleep.

appearance.notes: the Tallymen's slate-grey coat unbuttoned over a brass-buttoned waistcoat, the tally-book on a chain, boots off and set side by side

pockets.notes: the rogue's pickpocket lesson (first_rogue, the_strongbox): his house key and the purse he sleeps with his hand on

holds.notes: asleep on the boards beside his strongbox the night before tithe-day, through the rogue's three night lessons (a person stood up on a held spot plays the def's work_clip, not the hold's clip, so both say Sleep_Idle)

notes: Stood only for the rogue's night lessons, asleep by the strongbox that holds his tithe-book (docs/FIGHTING_STYLE_STARTS.md 3.4: 'pickpocketing the sleeping collector's key'). From first grey he is awake and out of the world, in the story's words; after it, sitting on the boards saying nothing.

name: Tella Oul
bio: Moreva's night-watch for the Reed Council: walks the landing's south boards from dusk to the first grey with a pole-lantern, and counts the boats in off the channels by the sound of their poles.
lore: Tella Oul lost a boot in the reeds in spring chasing somebody she is sure was a Tallyman's thief and nobody else is sure was anybody. She has kept the other boot, on a peg in the watch-hut, as evidence.
unique_habit: Stops dead every few paces and listens with her head on one side, lantern held away from her face so it does not blind her, and starts again when the channel has told her whatever it tells her.

appearance.notes: the Reed Council's indigo sash over an oiled cape, one good boot and one borrowed, a pole-lantern hooded on the landward side

holds.notes: at the head of the way down to the South Channel's traps, looking down it to the water, before dawn, from the first lesson (the box) through the second: carrying the book past her

schedule.notes: the night-watch at the head of the way down to the South Channel

perception.notes: the watch is her trade: a long look (24 m on a clear night, 18 in the Delta's mist, 13 in fog) and quick to be sure of what she sees; a crouched body in the dark six metres in front of her lantern is Seen in about three seconds, fifteen metres off it takes three times as long
